title: Onboarding telemetry privacy & security review (Hosted API guided onboarding) — v1
author: Marcus Lin
content:
## Summary
This document records the privacy and security review for the **Guided onboarding checklist** telemetry used to measure onboarding completion and validate certain checklist steps for the **Hosted API** (Phase 1).

**Outcome:** Approved to proceed to beta/GA **provided the requirements in this review are met** (noted as MUST/SHOULD below). The primary constraint is strict **data minimization** and an explicit prohibition on collecting **customer prompt content** or other sensitive payload data.

**Key decisions**
- Telemetry MUST be limited to **event names + allowlisted properties** needed for product analytics and checklist validation.
- Telemetry MUST NOT include **prompt content, completions, embeddings vectors, tool arguments, headers, request bodies, or user-entered free text**.
- Identity MUST use Redwood identifiers (org_id, project_id, actor_id) and MUST NOT attempt to fingerprint end-users.
- Raw event retention is time-bounded; long-lived reporting MUST use aggregated datasets.

## Scope
### In scope
- Console UI events for checklist interactions (view, click, step expanded, deep-link click, completion UI changes)
- Backend-generated signals for step validation (e.g., first successful API request, first streaming session)
- Funnel analytics datasets and dashboards derived from these events
- Access controls, retention, deletion and residency posture for telemetry and derived datasets

### Out of scope
- Dedicated/Private deployment onboarding telemetry (separate review required)
- Customer application telemetry emitted from SDKs within customer runtime (not collected by Redwood)
- Content logging of API requests/responses (explicitly prohibited for onboarding telemetry)

## Data classification
- **Telemetry events:** Internal operational/analytics data; may include **pseudonymous identifiers** and low-risk metadata.
- **Identifiers:** org_id/project_id/actor_id are considered **customer-sensitive** in aggregate (enable correlation). Treat as restricted.
- **Prohibited categories:** customer prompt/content, secrets, access tokens, API keys, raw IP addresses beyond security logging needs, and any end-user personal data (names/emails) unless already part of Redwood account identity and strictly required.

## Event collection overview
Telemetry supports two use cases:
1) **Checklist measurement:** completion rates, drop-off, time-to-first-success (TTFS), time-to-first-production-launch.
2) **Checklist validation:** marking steps complete when verifiable signals occur.

### Systems involved (high-level)
- **Redwood Console (web):** emits UI events via telemetry SDK.
- **Console backend services:** emit server-side validation events when computing step signals.
- **Telemetry pipeline:** ingestion → validation/allowlist → redaction → storage → datasets.
- **Analytics:** dashboards for DevEx/Product; alerts for telemetry health.

## Telemetry inventory (allowlisted properties)
The following is the **allowlist** for onboarding telemetry v1. Any property not listed here MUST be dropped at ingestion.

Table: Allowed event properties (v1)
- Required common properties (all events):
  - event_name (string)
  - event_time (RFC3339)
  - org_id (string; Redwood internal UUID)
  - project_id (string; Redwood internal UUID; may be null for org-level pages)
  - actor_id (string; Redwood internal UUID; Console user)
  - session_id (string; randomly generated; rotates on logout/timeout)
  - source (enum: console|backend)
  - environment (enum: prod|staging)
  - region (enum: us-east|us-west|eu-central|ap-southeast; see Residency)
  - dedupe_key (string; idempotency/deduplication)

- Optional allowed properties (event-specific):
  - checklist_id (string; fixed value for Phase 1, e.g., hosted_api_onboarding_v1)
  - step_id (string; from static step registry)
  - step_state (enum: not_started|in_progress|complete|skipped)
  - step_completion_method (enum: automatic|manual)
  - validation_signal (enum: first_successful_request|first_streaming_session|prod_api_key_created|usage_dashboard_visited)
  - http_status_family (enum: 2xx|4xx|5xx; MUST NOT include full status code if it increases fingerprinting risk)
  - error_category (enum: auth|quota|rate_limit|network|timeout|invalid_request|server_error|unknown)
  - sdk_language (enum: python|typescript|go|unknown) (only if derived from Redwood SDK user agent parsing; MUST NOT capture full UA)
  - docs_url_id (string; internal stable doc identifier, not full URL)
  - utm_campaign (string; fixed set for attribution; see Deep links)
  - is_new_org_cohort (boolean)
  - feature_flag_variant (string; e.g., control|checklist_enabled)
  - latency_bucket_ms (enum: lt200|200_500|500_1000|gt1000) (bucketed only)

**Explicitly disallowed properties**
- prompt, messages, completion, tool_arguments, function_call, embeddings, files, images, audio, any request/response payload
- api_key, authorization headers, cookies
- full URLs with query strings (to avoid leaking user-entered data); use docs_url_id + UTM campaign allowlist
- full IP addresses (not required for onboarding analytics)
- free-form strings entered by customers (project names, step notes, custom labels)
- stack traces, logs, exception messages that might contain payload fragments

## “No customer prompt content” constraint (hard requirement)
### Requirement
Onboarding telemetry MUST NOT include customer prompts or model outputs, even in truncated, hashed, or redacted form.

### Rationale
- Customer prompts may contain personal data, confidential business data, regulated information, or secrets.
- Hashing does not remove sensitivity and may enable correlation attacks.
- Telemetry for onboarding success does not require payload inspection.

### Enforcement controls
MUST:
1) **Property allowlist at ingestion** (drop unknown properties).
2) **Server-side guardrails**: lint/validation checks in telemetry libraries to prevent payload fields.
3) **Sampling-safe design**: do not rely on “sampling” to reduce risk; prohibited data must be blocked entirely.
4) **Automated tests**: unit tests validating allowlist behavior; regression tests for common payload keys.
5) **Code review checklist**: any PR touching telemetry must include a privacy checklist section.

## Identity model and user privacy
- actor_id represents an authenticated Redwood Console user (admin/member). No collection of end-user identity from customer applications.
- Do not collect customer employee emails or names in telemetry events. Account system retains those separately under standard policies.
- session_id is ephemeral and rotates; it is used only for funnel/session analytics.

### Cross-dataset linking constraints
- Joining onboarding telemetry to billing, support tickets, or request logs is permitted only via org_id/project_id under access controls described below.
- Any new join use case (e.g., automated “at-risk” scoring) requires an updated privacy review.

## Step validation signals (backend)
Checklist validations use **derived signals** rather than raw request payloads.

Approved validation mechanisms:
- First successful request: derived from gateway metrics/log counters (2xx observed) keyed by project_id.
- First streaming session: derived from streaming session lifecycle metrics (stream opened + first token delivered) without payload.
- Prod-mode API key created: derived from key management audit event (key created, key type=prod) without key material.
- Usage dashboard visited: derived from Console route visit event.

Constraints:
- Validation computations MUST NOT require reading prompt content.
- If request logs are used as the source of truth, extraction MUST be done on pre-existing metadata fields only (project_id, response class, timestamps), not body.

## Data residency and cross-region handling
### Residency posture (Phase 1)
- Telemetry events are ingested in-region (US/EU/APAC where applicable) and stored in the same region’s telemetry storage by default.
- Aggregated datasets may be replicated for centralized reporting **only if** they contain no user-level event rows and conform to the aggregation requirements below.

### Approved replication
- Aggregated daily funnel metrics (counts, medians, percentiles by cohort) may be replicated cross-region.
- Any replication of raw events across regions is NOT approved without a new review.

### EU considerations
- EU region telemetry storage must remain in the EU for raw events.
- Access from non-EU staff is controlled via just-in-time approval (see Access Controls) and must be auditable.

## Retention and deletion
Retention is designed to support onboarding measurement while minimizing risk.

### Retention schedule (approved)
- Raw onboarding telemetry events:
  - Default retention: **30 days**
  - Purpose: debugging onboarding instrumentation, near-term funnel iteration
  - Storage: region-local

- Derived, privacy-minimized analytics datasets:
  - Retention: **13 months** (supports quarterly comparisons and seasonality)
  - Data must be aggregated (no per-actor rows).

- Telemetry health metrics (pipeline-level):
  - Retention: **90 days**
  - Contains no customer identifiers beyond coarse region/environment.

### Deletion requests
- Customer-requested deletion is handled at the account level under Redwood’s standard processes.
- For onboarding telemetry, deletion is primarily time-based. If a customer requests deletion of identifiable telemetry before expiry:
  - We can delete by org_id/project_id within raw event storage for the active retention window.
  - Aggregated datasets are not designed for deletion-by-org; they should not contain small-cell counts that could re-identify.

MUST: Implement suppression for “small cells” in aggregated datasets (e.g., do not report cohorts with < 10 orgs).

## Access control and auditing
### Who can access what
- Raw events (30d):
  - Access limited to: Telemetry platform on-call (Engineering), Security, and specifically approved Analytics engineers for debugging.
  - Product/DevEx may access only via **pre-built dashboards** or aggregated datasets.

- Aggregated datasets (13mo):
  - Access for Product/DevEx/Engineering via analytics workspace roles.
  - No access to per-actor event rows.

### Controls
MUST:
- Enforce RBAC groups for telemetry stores (least privilege).
- Require SSO + MFA for any direct access.
- Maintain audit logs of queries against raw event tables (who/when/what).
- Use just-in-time elevation for exceptional access to raw event data (time-boxed, ticket-linked).

## Security controls
MUST:
- Encrypt telemetry data at rest and in transit.
- Ensure ingestion endpoints validate schemas and reject oversized payloads.
- Apply strict service-to-service auth (mTLS/service identity) between Console/backend and telemetry ingestion.
- Monitor for unexpected property keys and volume spikes (potential exfil/mis-instrumentation).

SHOULD:
- Add detection for high-entropy strings in allowed fields (e.g., accidental tokens in dedupe_key) and quarantine.

## Deep links to docs (UTM and URL hygiene)
- Console deep links must use stable doc identifiers and/or version-stable URLs.
- Telemetry must capture only docs_url_id and an allowlisted utm_campaign value.
- Do not capture full URL query strings.

## Risk assessment and mitigations
Primary risks:
1) **Accidental payload capture** via error objects, request logging, or exception messages.
   - Mitigation: allowlist + automated tests + lint rules + code review checklist.
2) **Linkability** across datasets leading to inference about customer behavior.
   - Mitigation: restrict raw access; aggregated datasets only; small-cell suppression.
3) **Cross-region replication** of EU raw telemetry.
   - Mitigation: explicit pipeline guardrails; replication only for aggregated metrics.

## Implementation requirements (checklist)
Engineering MUST complete before expanding beyond limited beta:
- [MUST] Ingestion allowlist enforced for onboarding telemetry v1.
- [MUST] Redaction/drop rules for known dangerous keys (prompt/messages/completion/authorization/api_key/etc.).
- [MUST] Raw event retention set to 30 days with automated deletion.
- [MUST] EU raw telemetry region-local storage verified.
- [MUST] RBAC groups configured for raw vs aggregated access.
- [MUST] Audit logs enabled for raw event queries.
- [MUST] Small-cell suppression in dashboards/exports.
- [SHOULD] Automated anomaly alerting for schema drift and missing events.

## Verification and ongoing compliance
- Telemetry platform team will run a weekly audit during beta to confirm:
  - no disallowed properties observed
  - retention deletion jobs operating
  - dashboard counts align with expected cohorts
- Any schema changes require Security review approval and an updated version number.

## Approvals

## Appendix A — Examples of safe vs unsafe payloads
Safe (allowed):
- event_name=onboarding_step_completed
- step_id=first_successful_request
- validation_signal=first_successful_request
- latency_bucket_ms=200_500

Unsafe (MUST be blocked):
- messages=[{"role":"user","content":"…"}]
- prompt="…"
- completion="…"
- request_body="…"
- headers={"Authorization":"Bearer …"}

## Appendix B — Change log
- 2026-02-22: Finalized retention schedule (raw 30d; aggregated 13mo) and added EU replication constraints.
- 2026-02-18: Added explicit disallowed property list and small-cell suppression requirement.
- 2026-02-14: Initial draft based on onboarding telemetry event schema v1 and checklist validation plan.
